newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Egyptian envoy in Israel-PLO peace effort.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian envoy in Israel-PLO peace effort.

text.p: An Egyptian special envoy will meet separately with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Thursday in another bid to revive peacemaking.
Israel has said the Egyptian effort was producing some progress but Palestinians said they did not expect a breakthrough and accused Israel of bargaining in bad faith.

"We appreciate the Egyptian role but at the same time we have no illusions," said Ahmed Abdel-Rahman, general-secretary of Arafat's Palestinian Authority cabinet, ahead of envoy Osama el-Baz's 1.30 p.m. (1030 GMT) meeting with Netanyahu.

"Netanyahu is carrying out a game of public relations that aims to show false flexibility with the Egyptian initiative," he told Reuters, referring to reports Israel might freeze Jewish settlement construction in Jerusalem and the rest of the West Bank, the main bone of contention between Israel and the PLO.
Netanyahu has denied the reports, vowing to press ahead with a huge housing project on a hill in Arab East Jerusalem which plunged peacemaking into crisis in March.

El-Baz, an adviser to Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, was hoping to arrange another meeting between Palestinian and Israeli negotiators who this week held their first talks since the peacemaking became deadlocked.
His meeting with Arafat was scheduled for 5 p.m. (1400 GMT).
Egypt, which sees itself as an unofficial sponsor of the Middle East peace process, launched the mediation effort last month after U.S. envoy Dennis Ross failed to revive peace talks.
Palestinians refuse to return to substantive negotiations until Israel halts settlement activities in the West Bank and and Gaza Strip.

Netanyahu -- who after taking office a year ago lifted a partial freeze on Jewish settlement imposed by the prior dovish government he ousted in elections -- says the construction does not violate peace deals.
The Israeli prime minister wants Arafat to crack down on Islamic militants.
"It is unlikely that a three-way meeting will take place before the weekend," said a senior Israeli official, who did not want to be identified.

El-Baz and Israeli officials said at the end of Sunday's talks that some progress had been made but Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat insisted the meeting did not mean the sides had resumed negotiations.
Israel occupied East Jerusalem in 1967 and claimed the whole city as its capital in a move not recognised internationally. Palestinians want East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state.
Palestinian officials on Thursday slammed a U.S. House of Representatives resolution this week recognising all of Jerusalem as Israel's capital.
"This decision will leave a dark shadow on security and stability in the Middle East and in Palestine. It is a clear call for violence and settlements," said Abdel-Rahman.
Israel called it a clear expression of American will.
"The majority of the world cannot ignore the fact that the American people has expressed its will in this most explicit and clear manner," said Netanyahu's adviser, David Bar-Illan.

House Speaker Newt Gingrich outraged Palestinians this week by describing the Palestinian Authority's decision to impose the death penalty against Arabs who sold land to Jews as "the kind of action we identify with Nazis".
"I had hoped that he would verify his facts and would ensure his statements would not smack of racism...but would be based on real facts," said Palestinian legislator Hanan Ashrawi.
